Train a student on a teacher's softened outputs instead of hard labels. The idea resurfaces in this story four separate times, each time in a new costume.

# Daily Digest — 2026-08-27 (window: 1 day)

## Use

_No items._

## Prototype

- **Real-time Unsupervised Object Discovery from Asynchronous Event Streams** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26644v1))
  Tracks: Datasets & Benchmarks
  Reason: Training-free, real-time moving-object discovery straight from the event stream: a linear-time probabilistic event filter for denoising plus Morton-code clustering that avoids a distance matrix, with code published and results on the public E-MLB benchmark. No training and no labels means we can measure it on our own data in an afternoon, which is exactly what we want from an event-camera evaluation.
  Action: Clone github.com/PrathamShenwai/SPEF_EMCC, run SPEF+EMCC on E-MLB and on any event capture we have, and record throughput and false-positive rate on static clutter.

## Evaluate

- **A Geometry-Driven, Framework-Agnostic Optimization for Object Pose Estimation** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26859v1))
  Tracks: 3D Geometry & Reconstruction, Datasets & Benchmarks
  Reason: Data-level fix for the ambiguity that quietly wrecks pose training on machined parts: canonicalise object rotation to the principal axes derived from inertial properties, which resolves symmetric-object label confusion before the network sees it. Framework-agnostic by construction, so it is cheap to test on an existing pipeline. Claims are on standard pose benchmarks, not industrial parts.
  Action: Read the PDF; if the canonicalisation is as framework-agnostic as claimed, re-label one symmetric-part pose set with principal axes and measure the change on our current model.
- **Data-efficient crack quantification in lithium-ion cathodes using foundation model transfer** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27162v1))
  Tracks: Industrial Vision Inspection, Vision Foundation Models
  Reason: Defect quantification done the way we would have to do it: a frozen self-supervised ViT encoder with a small trainable decoder plus iterative model-assisted annotation, applied to 120-megapixel electron-microscopy cross-sections where expert pixel labelling costs hours per image. It separates intragranular from intergranular cracking at population scale. Materials science rather than production inspection, and no code, but the annotation-budget recipe is the transferable part.
  Action: Read the annotation loop and the tiling strategy; consider replicating frozen-encoder + light-decoder on one of our own sparse-label defect sets.
- **Camera Calibration Using Inaccurate and Asynchronous Discrete GPS Trajectory from Drones** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26548v1))
  Tracks: Calibration & Camera Models, Synthetic Data & Simulation, Datasets & Benchmarks
  Reason: Target-free extrinsic calibration of a fixed camera from a moving object's noisy trajectory, solving the practical mess honestly: unknown GPS altitude bias and unknown camera-to-GPS time offset are estimated jointly with yaw/pitch/roll, and the discrete trajectory is interpolated with velocity. That is the same estimator shape as our camera-robot temporal calibration, with a cooperative target we can already fly or move.
  Action: Read the parameter-estimation formulation and the interpolation scheme; check the reported angular accuracy against a checkerboard-calibrated reference.
- **SSMB: Self-Supervised Local Feature Detection under Motion Blur** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27181v1))
  Tracks: 3D Geometry & Reconstruction, Robotics Vision
  Reason: Keypoint repeatability under motion blur, learned self-supervised without a deblur pass and without regressing a handcrafted detector's opinions. Moving parts and moving cameras are our normal condition, and blur is where our matching front-ends degrade quietly. No code announced.
  Action: Read the PDF; check whether the detector is drop-in for our matching front-end and whether repeatability is reported against SIFT/SuperPoint on real blur.
- **GeoMAD: Geometry-Aware Multi-View Anomaly Detection via Deformable Fusion and Distributional Alignment** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26724v1))
  Tracks: Calibration & Camera Models, 3D Geometry & Reconstruction, Industrial Vision Inspection
  Reason: Multi-view, multi-class industrial anomaly detection - directly our domain. The claim worth checking is that continuous cross-view deformable fusion beats both voxel reconstruction and discrete patch matching, i.e. you can get geometric awareness without building 3D. No code link.
  Action: Read the PDF; compare the reported multi-class numbers against our current single-view inspection baseline and see what the fusion module costs at inference.

## Watch

- **Parameter Efficient Continual Learning for Sparse Event-Based Transformers** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26720v1))
  Tracks: 3D Sensors, Edge AI & Deployment
  Reason: Continual learning on sparse spiking event transformers with a frozen backbone and low-rank adapters - the right target (adapt at the edge under memory and energy limits) but early: no measured energy or latency on real neuromorphic hardware in the abstract.
  Action: No action; track whether event-based edge models start reporting on-device numbers.
- **NeuDonatello: Uncertainty-Aware Framework for Accurate Neural SDF Learning** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26504v1))
  Tracks: 3D Geometry & Reconstruction
  Reason: Uncertainty-aware neural SDF reconstruction - models spatially varying SDF uncertainty by Monte Carlo sampling and strengthens regularisation exactly where RGB supervision is unreliable (textureless, occluded). Confidence per surface point is what a measurement pipeline needs; the evaluation is reconstruction-quality, not error budget, and no code is mentioned.
  Action: Watch for code; the reusable idea is the uncertainty-weighted regulariser, not the SDF framework.
- **Comparative Evaluation of 3D Reconstruction Methods for Immersive Visualization of Laboratory Objects** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27301v1))
  Tracks: 3D Geometry & Reconstruction, 3D Sensors, Industrial Vision Inspection
  Reason: Compares photogrammetry, NeRF, 3DGS and LiDAR on the objects that actually break scanners - transparent, reflective, low-texture - and reports NeRF most consistent. But fidelity is rated subjectively by graduate students for holographic teaching material, with no geometric error anywhere, so it is not evidence for a scanning decision.
  Action: No action; treat the transparent/reflective ranking as a hypothesis to test with real metrology, not a result.
- **DPA-I2P: Depth-Guided Projective Alignment for Image-to-Point-Cloud Registration in Autonomous Driving** ([link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26589v1))
  Tracks: 3D Geometry & Reconstruction, 3D Sensors, Edge AI & Deployment
  Reason: Image-to-point-cloud registration is the camera-LiDAR extrinsic problem wearing a driving hat: estimate camera pose inside a sparse LiDAR map via learned cross-modal correspondence, with ray-conditioned metric depth as the bridge. The idea transfers, the model does not - it is trained end-to-end on driving data and there is no code.
  Action: No action now; if we take on camera-LiDAR alignment, read the ray-conditioned depth encoding first.

## Ignore (15)

Representative titles:
- 4DSynth: Controllable Procedural World Synthesis for Dynamic Embodied Simulation
- FAN-LoRA: A Fourier-Adaptive Nonlinear Low-Rank Adaptor for Medical Foundation Model Domain Adaptation
- KnockGS:interaction-Grounded Calibrationof Physical Gaussian Representations

But fidelity is rated subjectively by graduate students for holographic teaching material, with no geometric error anywhere, so it is not evidence for a scanning decision.
  Action: No action; treat the transparent/reflective ranking as a hypothesis to test with real metrology, not a result.
